claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements and have disordered lattice structures.
Local atomic-environment metrics and disorder parameters influence phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Local structure, chemical disorder, and bonding characteristics have nonlinear, interdependent effects on phonon scattering.
A graph neural network can learn the effects of local structure, chemical disorder, and bonding characteristics on phonon scattering.
Incorporating local bonding descriptors, disorder indices, and phonon density-of-states fingerprints will improve prediction of phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed graph neural network will map phonon density of states more accurately than traditional models.
The proposed graph neural network will predict phonon scattering rates more accurately than traditional models.
The proposed model will identify high-entropy alloys with ultralow phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed model will achieve at least a 20% improvement in prediction accuracy over standard DFT-Boltzmann transport approaches.
Standard DFT-Boltzmann predictions do not fully account for disorder-induced phonon scattering.
The model is applicable to high-entropy alloys whose compositions are represented in its training dataset.
The model is applicable at room temperature and moderately elevated temperatures represented during training.
Prediction reliability may decrease for compositions with local atomic environments substantially different from those in the training dataset.
Prediction reliability may decrease at temperatures outside the range represented in model training.
Model performance depends on the representativeness of the training dataset.
